findings.title: Compat alias `family` injected by normalizer but callers never read canonical `filename_prefix`
findings.suggested_fix: The compat alias is introduced at line 995 with a comment saying step 11 will remove it. However, every downstream call site reads `action_spec.get('family', ...)` or `action_spec['family']` (lines 1037, 1054, 1123, 2746, 2806, 3472, 3515, 3567) -- none reads `filename_prefix`. The normalizer performs a rename into a new canonical field (`filename_prefix`) but then also unconditionally re-writes `family` with the same value, meaning callers get no migration pressure and the canonical field never actually becomes the authoritative read path. The compat alias is structurally indistinguishable from the pre-migration state. Step 11 has no forcing function. Track a TODO or assertion that fails if `family` is read without the alias being explicitly enabled, or invert: make callers read `filename_prefix` now and alias `family = filename_prefix` only in the JSON response boundary.

findings.title: `prefix_catalog` entries carry duplicate `preview_xp`/`l0_ref` data that is not validated by the normalizer
findings.suggested_fix: For the `player` prefix, `prefix_catalog.player.preview_xp` (line 57) and `prefix_catalog.player.l0_ref` (line 59) are identical to `template_sets.player_native_idle_only.actions.idle.preview_xp` (line 175) and `l0_ref` (line 177), and again duplicated in `player_native_full.actions.idle` (lines 208-211). The same duplication exists for `attack` and `plydie`. `_normalize_template_registry` validates and normalizes only `template_sets.*.actions`; `prefix_catalog` entries are passed through as raw dicts. If a sha256 is updated in one location and not the other the registry silently carries contradictory integrity data. Either make `prefix_catalog` entries reference their corresponding `template_sets` action (eliminating the copy), or extend the normalizer to validate `prefix_catalog` entries against the same field contract it applies to action specs.

findings.title: `_load_reference_l0` and `_load_reference_l1` duplicate the registry scan loop
findings.suggested_fix: Both functions (lines 1043-1080 and 1106-1138) contain an identical nested loop: iterate `template_sets` -> `actions`, find the action where `act.get('family') == family`, extract `l0_ref`. The only difference is that `_load_reference_l0` also extracts `l0_ref_sha256` and validates the checksum. Extract a helper `_find_l0_ref_path(reg, family) -> tuple[str|None, str|None]` that returns `(l0_ref_path, l0_ref_sha256)` and call it from both. This also makes the sha256 check available to `_load_reference_l1` if it ever needs it, and means a single change to the lookup logic covers both callers.

findings.title: Hardcoded family whitelist at line 2470 diverges from `ENABLED_FAMILIES` constant and registry data
findings.suggested_fix: Line 2470 contains `if family not in ("player", "attack", "plydie")` -- a literal tuple of family names. The same filtering is done elsewhere via `if family not in ENABLED_FAMILIES` (lines 2747, 2807, 3516, 3568). With the new schema, the authoritative list of enabled, authorable families is now derivable from `prefix_catalog` + `skin_family_scope`. The literal tuple at line 2470 will silently exclude any future authorable family that gets added to the registry but not to this hardcoded list. Replace with `ENABLED_FAMILIES` or derive from the loaded registry.

findings.title: `_normalize_template_action_spec` accepts `preview_xp` falling back to `l0_ref` silently
findings.suggested_fix: Line 963: `preview_xp = str(spec.get('preview_xp') or spec.get('l0_ref') or '').strip()`. Similarly line 964 falls back sha256. This means if `preview_xp` is absent, the normalizer silently uses `l0_ref` as the preview path without emitting any warning or diagnostic. The missing-fields list at lines 968-985 will NOT flag this as missing because the value is filled in. A future schema entry that genuinely lacks `preview_xp` (because its first frame coincidentally equals L0) will get a correct-looking spec, and the mistake will only surface visually. The silent coercion disguises schema gaps. Either reject missing `preview_xp` outright (it is present in all current entries), or emit a logged warning when the fallback path is used.

findings.title: Test `test_template_registry_actions_are_normalized` hardcodes `skin_family == 'human'` for all actions
findings.suggested_fix: Line 29 asserts `action['skin_family'] == 'human'` unconditionally for every action in the registry. The registry already includes a `green` skin family scope, and future template sets may have `skin_family: 'green'` actions. When that happens this assertion will fail for a correct registry, forcing a test edit instead of finding a real bug. Replace with `assert action['skin_family'] in registry.get('skin_family_scope', {})` to validate that the value is a known scope key rather than pinning it to one literal.

findings.title: `bundle_contract.mjs` reads raw JSON without any normalization layer
findings.suggested_fix: The JS module reads `template_registry.json` directly (line 13) and accesses `spec.filename_prefix` and `spec.skin_family` (lines 51-52) with no normalization step. The Python loader normalizes on load, injecting canonical fields and the `family` compat alias. The JS loader does not. If the registry ever has a v1-style entry with `family` instead of `filename_prefix`, the JS path will return empty strings for those fields with no error. Either add a lightweight JS normalizer mirroring the Python one, or document explicitly that the JSON file is always schema_version 2 and these fields are guaranteed present, making the asymmetry a deliberate constraint rather than an invisible risk.

residual_risks: The `prefix_catalog` section is new and load-bearing for the `skin_family_scope` + mounted-family features, but has zero test coverage for its field-level integrity (no test validates sha256 values, runtime_role presence, or that `template_actions` cross-references resolve to real template_set/action_key pairs).

The compat alias `spec['family'] = filename_prefix` is written unconditionally, so a registry entry that legitimately sets `family` to a different value than `filename_prefix` would be silently overwritten at load time. There is no assertion or warning that the two are consistent in the raw JSON.
The `schema_version` sentinel at lines 1019-1020 defaults to 2 if absent, meaning a corrupted or zero-version file would be treated as valid v2 schema and pass normalization without error.
testing_gaps: No test validates that `prefix_catalog` sha256 values match the actual files on disk (only `template_sets.*.actions` paths are checked in `test_template_registry_reference_paths_exist`, lines 36-38; `prefix_catalog` path existence is checked at lines 40-42 but sha256 is not).
No test exercises the compat-alias path where the raw registry contains `family` instead of `filename_prefix`, verifying that normalization correctly maps it.
No test covers the `_normalize_template_action_spec` `preview_xp` fallback-to-`l0_ref` branch.
No test validates cross-references from `prefix_catalog[key].template_actions[*].{template_set_key, action_key}` against the actual keys present in `template_sets`.
No test covers registry load behavior when `schema_version` is absent from the JSON.
